item.title: The Strength of Root Cuts in an Extended Abstract Branch-and-Cut Model
item.description: arXiv:2610.31774v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The branch-and-cut paradigm has led to effective solvers for a wide range of mathematical optimization problems. Despite significant theoretical work on pure branching and pure cutting, less is known about their interaction. We study an extended abstract branch-and-cut model to investigate tradeoffs between branching and cutting, including the time to generate cuts. We prove that, under symmetric branching, some minimal-time tree has all cuts at the root, before the first branching node, and that there is an asymmetric setting where some minimal-time tree has no internal cuts, i.e., cuts both preceded and followed by branching. For other settings, although a root-cut tree may be suboptimal and differ substantially in structure from a minimal-time tree, it nevertheless provides a reliable approximation whose tree time does not deviate arbitrarily from the optimum. For constant cut strength and bounded time functions, we show that the best root-cut tree is asymptotically optimal as the target bound grows. In addition, under a single-cut-per-path restriction, we characterize when some minimal-time tree has an internal cut. Lastly, simulations indicate that the best root-cut tree is much closer to a minimal-time tree than our worst-case approximation guarantee suggests.
item.dc:creator: Boyang Han, Aleksandr M. Kazachkov

item.title: Rapid stabilization for Stokes and Navier-Stokes systems with localized disturbance
item.description: arXiv:2610.31790v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In this study, we analyze the rapid stabilization of Stokes and the two- and three-dimensional Navier-Stokes systems in the presence of an unknown spatially localized disturbance. A multivalued feedback control strategy is proposed which combines the Lyapunov frequency method with the multivalued sign operator. This methodology connects Lyapunov-based stability analysis with spectral inequalities, while the inclusion of the sign operator provides robustness against disturbance. The closed-loop system is governed by a differential inclusion, for which well-posedness is proved via the theory of maximal monotone operators. This approach guarantees global rapid exponential stabilization for the Stokes system and local rapid exponential stabilization for the two- and three-dimensional Navier-Stokes systems, with arbitrarily large disturbance bounds. In three dimensions, we obtain global strong solutions and rapid exponential stabilization for initial data sufficiently small in the $L^2$-norm with a prescribed, arbitrarily large bound in the $H^1$-norm.
item.dc:creator: Christian Calle, Patricio Guzm\'an, Hugo Parada, Jefferson Prada

item.title: Observability from measurable sets for strongly coupled parabolic systems
item.description: arXiv:2610.31876v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We characterize observability of strongly coupled parabolic systems from arbitrary space-time measurable sets of positive measure. For constant coercive diffusion matrices and arbitrary constant zeroth-order coupling and observation matrices, observability holds if and only if the generalized Kalman rank condition is satisfied at every Dirichlet eigenvalue. The diffusion matrix need not be diagonalizable, and the number of components is arbitrary. The observation is measured in $L^1$, yielding null controllability with bounded controls by duality. The proof combines a Remez-type inequality for exponential polynomials with a quantitative analysis of the mode-dependent Kalman condition. The resulting finite-dimensional observability estimate is uniform over the spatial modes up to a polynomial frequency loss. A spectral inequality and the Lebeau--Robbiano strategy then give observability of the full system.
item.dc:creator: Xinyi Chen, K\'evin Le Balc'h

item.title: Closed-form Optimal Solutions for Propulsive-Differential Drag Control of Spacecraft Swarms
item.description: arXiv:2610.31970v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: This paper presents a novel optimal control approach for Distributed Space Systems (DSS) to minimize the total delta-v cost for large, time-constrained reconfigurations. Reconfiguration cost is decreased by blending differential drag and propulsive control within the same control window. By parameterizing the problem with Relative Orbital Elements (ROE) and leveraging reachable set theory, a maneuver planning methodology is derived to produce provably-optimal, full roto-translational control solutions in closed-form, such that they can be implemented on hardware-limited spacecraft.
item.arxiv:journal_reference: Proceedings of the 2022 AAS/AIAA Astrodynamics Specialist Conference, Charlotte, North Carolina, August 7-11 2022
item.dc:creator: Matthew Hunter, Simone D'Amico

item.title: Closed-form Optimal Propulsive-Differential Drag Control for Large Reconfigurations of Spacecraft Swarms
item.description: arXiv:2610.31973v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Distributed Space Systems offer unique capabilities but have significant hardware limitations on computational processing and fuel when employing small satellites. These constraints drive interest in deterministic maneuver planning that incorporates orbital perturbations to improve final state accuracy and decrease reconfiguration delta-v cost. This paper proposes a novel closed-form, provably optimal framework to generate complete roto-translational solutions for propulsive-differential drag control of multiple satellites. The approach leverages relative orbit elements and reachable set theory to characterize all control with a single methodology that can be readily generalized to generic impulsive-continuous control. The algorithm is robust to large reconfigurations and extended control windows where differential drag is most effective.

item.title: Optimal Graphon Control of Collective Dynamics
item.description: arXiv:2610.31975v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study optimal control of non-linear graphon dynamics in which the interaction kernel itself is the control. Motivated by opinion formation in social networks, we ask how changing who influences whom can steer a population toward a desired outcome. We develop a framework using interaction kernels with bounded variation in the receiver label, providing compactness while accommodating finite networks. We prove existence of an optimal pair and show that finite-agent approximations recover the continuum optimal value under successive refinement of the network and initial data, with subsequential convergence of suitably chosen discrete optimizers. Numerical experiments use neural networks to approximate optimal controls for bounded-confidence and graphon Kuramoto dynamics, illustrating how changes in interactions can prevent fragmentation and promote synchronization.
item.dc:creator: Joseph K. Miller, Brandon Su

item.title: A Globally Convergent Newton Method for Nonsmooth Optimization in the absence of Smooth Surrogates
item.description: arXiv:2610.31992v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We propose a globally convergent Newton method for convex composite optimization problems with polyhedral regularizers. The method rests on the observation that the proximal gradient step yields not only a new point but also a subgradient, which determines the face on which the linearization of the regularizer is exact. Minimizing a second-order model of the objective over this face produces a Newton direction that involves no generalized second-order information about the regularizer and is a descent direction for the objective itself. The method is therefore globalized by an Armijo line search on the original objective which, unlike forward-backward envelope techniques, requires only evaluations of the smooth component. We establish global convergence and local quadratic convergence to tilt-stable minimizers without any nondegeneracy condition, and show that the unit step is always accepted when the smooth component is quadratic, which yields a line-search-free method. The subproblems require only projections onto faces, which are explicit for the Lasso and nonnegative least squares and computable in linear time for the fused Lasso. Numerical experiments show that the method compares favorably with state-of-the-art solvers.
item.dc:creator: Tran T. A. Nghia, Nghia V. Vo, Khoa V. H. Vu

item.title: Strengthening AC optimal power flow relaxation through offline bound tightening and linear approximations
item.description: arXiv:2610.32006v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The alternating-current optimal power flow (ACOPF) problem is fundamental to power system operation and planning, but its nonconvexity makes globally optimal solutions of large-scale instances computationally challenging. Convex relaxations provide tractable lower bounds for assessing solution quality and supporting global optimization, although their effectiveness depends strongly on relaxation strength. This paper proposes an offline convexification and bound tightening framework for constructing strong linear programming (LP) relaxations for families of related ACOPF instances. Rather than repeating the tightening procedure for each instance, we compute variable bounds and second-order cone outer-approximation (SOC-OA) cuts offline using a demand-slack model and reuse them for subsequent instances with the same topology and admissible demand variations. Computational results on PGLib instances show that the fully offline approach achieves an average gap of $4.32\%$, compared with $3.80\%$ for the fully online approach, while achieving an average speedup of approximately $272\times$. The results demonstrate that offline convexification and bound tightening can recover most of the relaxation improvement of online tightening while significantly reducing the computational burden for repeated ACOPF evaluations.
item.dc:creator: Xiangxin An, Constance Crozier, Santanu S. Dey

item.title: On Exact Critical-Region Boundaries in Continuous-Time Multiparametric Optimal Control Problems
item.description: arXiv:2610.32043v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Continuous-time multiparametric model predictive control solves the optimal control problem once, offline, for every initial state, and divides the initial-state space into critical regions, each with its own control law and sequence of active constraints. A boundary between two regions is either a hyperplane, given by one linear equation, or curved. The curved boundaries have not been computed to date; a classifier has been trained instead to distinguish the regions, so the partition has been known only approximately. In this paper we show that a curved boundary can be computed exactly, without solving any optimal control problem. The method rests on one property. Once the sequence of active constraints is fixed, together with the instants inside it at which a constraint becomes active or inactive (the switching times) and the instant at which the change of the neighboring region first appears (the event time), every condition on a boundary is a linear equation in the initial state, so the computation of a boundary, curved or not, is exact. We fix one of these instants, a switching time or the event time, and solve the linear equations that correspond to it for the corresponding initial state on the boundary; stepping the fixed instant along the horizon yields the whole boundary. A hyperplane is the case in which no instant is left to fix. We illustrate the method on the Newell-Lee evaporator, which has seven critical regions and eight boundaries, four hyperplanes and four curved, computing one boundary of each type in full with the adjacent regions at its ends.
item.dc:creator: Lida Lamakani, Efstratios N. Pistikopoulos

item.title: A Dynamic Inventory Rationing Model for Last-Mile Delivery of Medication in Liberia's Community Health Program
item.description: arXiv:2610.32051v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study the dynamic allocation of scarce medications in Liberia's community health program. A central warehouse supplies a health facility and the Community Health Assistants (CHAs) it supervises. When a CHA runs out of medication, patients are referred to the facility, incurring travel costs if they complete the referral and remain untreated otherwise. Allocating inventory to CHAs allows more patients to receive treatment without traveling, while retaining inventory centrally preserves flexibility to respond to uncertain demand. The allocation problem must balance these considerations while accounting for fairness across locations. We formulate this problem as a finite-horizon stochastic control problem whose objective combines the costs of referrals and untreated patients with a demand-weighted fairness utility. Because standard dynamic programming methods are computationally intractable in this setting, we develop a continuous-time approximation that involves controlling the drift rate of a reflected Brownian motion. We then adapt the deep splitting method, using deep neural networks to approximate the value function and its gradient and compute a dynamic allocation policy. We calibrate the model using data on malaria cases among children in the Fangonda region of Lofa County, Liberia, and evaluate the proposed policy in the original discrete-time model. In the baseline setting, our policy reduces operating costs by about 6% relative to the strongest benchmark, the fairness-only policy, while retaining approximately 98% of its fairness utility. Additional experiments show that higher referral costs shift inventory toward CHAs and reduce local unmet demand, while greater demand variability increases our policy's performance over the fairness-only benchmark. Our model and computational approach provide a framework for studying similar last-mile allocation problems.
item.dc:creator: Baris Ata, Yufan Chen, Robert Montgomery

item.title: Continuous-Time Wasserstein Distributionally Robust Control: Limits, Duality, and Stability
item.description: arXiv:2610.32080v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: A sampled robust control problem averages future values over disturbance laws, while its continuous-time counterpart evolves with an averaged drift. We establish a fluid limit connecting these two models for Wasserstein ambiguity sets. Under a uniform disturbance moment bound and subcritical growth, sampled Bellman values converge locally uniformly to the upper and lower values of a discounted differential game. The argument accommodates unbounded disturbances without requiring square-integrable increments. We also derive an explicit bound on the change in either game value when both the radius and center of the ambiguity set vary. For Euclidean disturbance space, uniform Lipschitz continuity in the disturbance, common state and cost Lipschitz bounds, and a discount rate exceeding the drift's state Lipschitz constant, this estimate converts distributional confidence bounds into uniform value approximation bounds. Static Wasserstein duality reformulates pointwise distributional optimization; affine disturbance dependence permits an exact reduction to a ball of means. Experiments illustrate the common limit and decreasing value error with sample size. For a nonlinear disturbance model, uniform shifts overestimate worst-case recovery speed by about 36\%. In a two-product inventory model, increasing ambiguity raises production near balance while reducing the region of full production in deeper backlogs.
item.dc:creator: Minjung Gim, Hee Jun Yang, Yeoneung Kim

item.title: Timed Recovery Safe Gradient Flows for Constrained Nonlinear Programming
item.description: arXiv:2610.32089v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: This paper studies how to relax pointwise feasibility in continuous-time dynamics for inequality-constrained nonlinear programming while retaining a quantitative feasible-recovery guarantee. Existing safe gradient flows enforce forward invariance of the feasible set, which yields an anytime-feasible dynamics but can be overly restrictive for optimization because it suppresses transient infeasible motion that may be essential for effective descent. To address this limitation, we propose a timed recovery safe gradient flow that replaces pointwise feasibility with fixed-horizon feasible recovery. The proposed construction augments the state with a timer that records the elapsed infeasible duration and computes a minimum-norm correction to the nominal gradient flow through a pointwise convex quadratic program. We show that the resulting augmented safe set is forward invariant and that every trajectory initialized from the feasible set returns to it within every time window of length \(\tau\). We further show that, in a strict interior inactive regime, the closed-loop dynamics reduces exactly to the nominal gradient flow and recovers the corresponding local convergence behavior. Numerical examples illustrate how the recovery horizon shapes the closed-loop behavior and corroborate the theoretical analysis.
item.dc:creator: Tianxi Luo, Yue Wu, Fei Chen, Hongsheng Qi

item.title: A branch-and-filter method for mixed-integer linear programming
item.description: arXiv:2610.32165v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We develop a new tree-search framework for mixed-integer linear programming problems, which incorporates a filter mechanism as a node-acceptance device. The introduced branch-and-filter algorithm combines proper branching actions with a filter on integrality violation and an incumbent-dependent objective coordinate. Inspired by classical filter methods in nonconvex constrained optimization, the proposed method moves to a restoration phase whenever sufficient progress cannot be provided by the filter and funnel mechanisms, the latter of which is anchored at global relaxation lower bounds. Under mild assumptions, the introduced method either certifies infeasibility in finitely many iterations, or converges to global optimality. Moreover, we establish a total outer iteration complexity bound of order $\mathcal{O}(\varepsilon^{-1})$ to certification of an $\varepsilon$-optimal mixed-integer solution through fixed-integer linear programming recovery. We finally perform several numerical experiments to study the performance of branch-and-filter against benchmark solvers, under a branch-and-bound, a branch-and-cut, and a novel cell-deletion realization of the proposed restoration oracle.
item.dc:creator: Nikos Dimou

item.title: Distributed Attacker Assignment and Interception Control in Multi-Agent Target-Attacker-Defender Games
item.description: arXiv:2610.32244v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: This paper addresses the Target-Attacker-Defender (TAD) game within a planar environment, focusing on the protection of a stationary target against incoming threats. To compensate for potential speed disadvantages of the defenders, we leverage geometric pre-positioning within an annular defense perimeter. The problem is formulated as an area interception problem, for which we propose a distributed multi-agent algorithm consisting of two primary modules: target allocation and interception control. For target allocation, an equitable region partitioning strategy is employed to divide the defense area into annular sectors and assign defenders to attackers. Under specified angular-separation and parameter conditions, the proposed partitioning mechanism ensures that each defender is assigned at most one attacker, thereby reducing the complexity of multi-agent assignment. For the control layer, movement protocols based on zero-sum differential games and coverage optimization are designed, achieving Nash equilibrium strategies while maintaining effective barrier coverage. Numerical simulations show that the proposed method enables slower defenders to intercept faster attackers through proactive deployment and maintains nearly constant local computation time as the swarm size increases.
item.dc:creator: Pengyang Fan, Shaoqing Zhang, Chao Zhai, Weiguo Xia

item.title: Continuous-Time Mean-Variance Portfolio Selection Reinforcement Learning Problems for a Markov Regime-Switching System with No-Shorting Constraints
item.description: arXiv:2610.32301v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: This paper is the first to study the continuous-time mean-variance portfolio selection problem with no-shorting constraints in a Markov regime-switching market using reinforcement learning (RL). The main challenge stems from the interaction between random regime shifts and portfolio non-negativity constraints, which typically causes the coupled Hamilton-Jacobi-Bellman (HJB) equations to lose smoothness across different state regions. Additionally, directly imposing no-shorting constraints on randomized policies disrupts their analytically tractable Gaussian structure, complicating both exploratory modeling and reinforcement learning. To address these challenges, we propose an auxiliary exploratory approach that limits the policy to a Gaussian distribution and applies the no-shorting constraint solely to its mean. We explicitly characterize the optimal policy for this auxiliary problem and demonstrate that, by appropriately selecting the exploration variance, its optimal mean policy exactly matches the optimal policy of the original constrained mean-variance problem. Building upon this analytical framework, we develop a model-free reinforcement learning algorithm that learns the optimal portfolio policy directly from trajectory data. Numerical experiments support the theoretical results and show that the proposed method can effectively recover the optimal no-shorting portfolio in a regime-switching market.
item.dc:creator: Minghui Zhang, Xun Li, Xin Zhang

item.title: A stochastic mirror descent algorithm for mean-field control problems
item.description: arXiv:2610.32303v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We develop a stochastic mirror descent method for continuous-time McKean-Vlasov control with measure-valued controls and general Bregman regularisation. The dependence on the state law leads to a coupled Wasserstein-Bregman stability problem and to a McKean-Vlasov adjoint equation, which have no counterpart in classical stochastic control. We establish a first-order representation of the cost and prove its relative smoothness in two regimes: nonlinear dynamics with bounded cost derivatives, and affine state-law dynamics with linearly growing cost derivatives, the latter covering linear-quadratic (LQ) and more general nonquadratic models. Our regularity conditions in the control measure are formulated through directional finite increments and do not require second-order flat derivatives. We further introduce relative semiconvexity along admissible forward-backward trajectories, allowing compensation between the dynamics, running cost, and terminal cost beyond pointwise Hamiltonian convexity. This yields energy dissipation, an O(1/n) convergence rate at the convexity threshold, and geometric convergence when regularisation dominates relative nonconvexity. Explicit LQ criteria and numerical experiments illustrate the scope of the results.
item.dc:creator: Noufel Frikha (CES), Aymen Haouas (X)

item.title: MIACE and Monotone Tracking: Exact Tuning for First-Order Plants and Positive Cascades with Pure Delay
item.description: arXiv:2610.32401v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The Module of Integral Absolute Complex Error (MIACE) was created by me 23 years ago. It gave very nice behaviour to the transient response of the controlled systems I tested. It combines absolute tracking-error and equilibrium-centered command areas. For a stable unit-gain plant with known pure delay, an exact identity separates squared MIACE excess into a negative-area penalty and a weighted area imbalance. The resulting lower bound depends on the plant's first low-frequency moment and the delay. Every attaining response of a positive cascade is monotone, independently of controller structure. For a first-order plant, output variation and peak overshoot also admit quantitative bounds. Exact conditions identify the unique positive PI controller attaining the delayed bound; filtered PID extends attainment beyond this PI range. For cascades of arbitrary order, Hermite interpolation and a finite-support delay remainder construct proper rational controllers of the same order, with internal exponential stability proved by positive convolution representations. An exponential-moment characterization then closes the attainment question when internal delay blocks are allowed: an ordinary command attains the bound if and only if $\alpha>\mu+\delta-1$. An explicit internal-model controller realizes every feasible weight and delay. A sharp amplitude-cap condition determines the least command peak among all attaining responses and the complete capped sign-preserving area front. A small-gain estimate supplies an explicit MIACE deviation bound under delay error. A storage balance also extends the exact MIACE identity and monotone attainment to a nonlinear first-order class without delay. Independent physical integrations retain delays exactly; quadratic comparisons provide complementary benchmarks.
item.dc:creator: Latchezar Tomov

item.title: On the Limits of Stochastic Push-Pull over Time-Varying Digraphs
item.description: arXiv:2610.32422v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Stochastic Push-Pull achieves linear speedup with respect to the network size $n$ on static strongly connected digraphs, but whether this speedup persists on time-varying networks remains unclear. In this work, we construct a quadratic decentralized problem on period-two networks showing that stochastic Push-Pull may fail to attain linear speedup over time-varying digraphs. For $p$-periodic networks, we identify an effective node count $n_{\mathrm{eff}}\le n$ that governs the leading stochastic term. Specifically, for smooth nonconvex objectives, we establish convergence upper bounds and matching lower bounds for stochastic Push-Pull with constant stepsizes, both exhibiting the leading-order dependence $\Theta(1/\sqrt{n_{\mathrm{eff}} T})$. When $p=1$, the identity $n_{\mathrm{eff}}=n$ recovers the usual linear speedup for static digraphs. However, periodic networks can have $n_{\mathrm{eff}}=o(n)$, demonstrating the loss of linear speedup under temporal variation. Numerical experiments illustrate effective-count scaling and the separation between static and periodic networks, consistent with our theoretical findings.
item.dc:creator: Feiming Wang, Yutong He, Sulaiman Alghunaim, Kun Yuan

item.title: On the closure under barycenters of location-scatter families with a normalized generator
item.description: arXiv:2610.32446v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We provide an example of a normalized absolutely continuous probability whose location-scatter family (LSF) does not contain all the 2-Wassertein geodesics passing through its elements. In particular, we find a counterexample for Corollary 4.5 in [2]. Finally, we prove that LSFs with a (possibly singular) radially symmetric generator are closed under 2-Wasserstein barycenters.
item.dc:creator: Pietro Aldrigo

item.title: Dual companions and improved regularity of Lagrange multipliers in optimal control
item.description: arXiv:2610.32520v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We investigate optimal control problems whose state equation takes the form $\mathcal{A}x-\mathcal{B}u=b$, where $\mathcal{A}:\mathcal{X}\to\mathcal{P}'$ is an isomorphism from a Banach state space $\mathcal{X}$ onto the dual of a reflexive Banach space $\mathcal{P}$. The adjoint equation involves the Banach space adjoint $\mathcal{A}':\mathcal{P}\to\mathcal{X}'$, so that, in general, state and multiplier are of different regularity. For particular classes of partial differential equations, the typically weaker regularity of the multiplier is improved a posteriori by bootstrapping. In this work, we provide an abstract foundation for this methodology on the operator level. More precisely, we show that whenever the state cost extends to a differentiable function on a Hilbert space $\mathcal{H}$ in which $\mathcal{X}$ is densely embedded, as for $L^2$-tracking costs on Sobolev-type state spaces, the multiplier automatically lies in a subspace of $\mathcal{P}$, the dual companion, on which $\mathcal{A}'$ restricts to an isomorphism onto $\mathcal{H}'$. This yields an optimality system with balanced regularity, where state and multiplier solve equations of the same type. In applications, the dual companion can be identified by integration by parts in time or space. We illustrate the framework by linear elliptic and parabolic equations, Cauchy problems governed by general $C_0$-semigroups, and a wave equation with accumulated-state observation.
item.dc:creator: Till Preuster, Manuel Schaller

item.title: Who pays for urban environment management? The role of the third-party service provider
item.description: arXiv:2610.32528v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The dominant contemporary paradigm of direct state-led urban environmental regulation entails significant risks, including high administrative burden, frequent conflicts with polluting entities, and economic vulnerabilities for those sources. To address these deficiencies, this paper integrates third-party service provider (TPSP) into China's existing management framework as a beneficial extension beyond conventional government intervention. Utilizing an evolutionary game approach, we compare two distinct institutional settings, a non-integration management mode and an integration management mode, and scrutinize the evolutionary dynamics across both two- and three-dimensional systems. To enhance system robustness, we embed a strategic behavior-based dynamic punishment mechanism that effectively eliminates the perturbing effects of varied penalty rules, thereby steering all stakeholders toward an ideal stable state. This comparative institutional analysis isolates the marginal contribution of third-party intermediation, specifies when outsourcing environmental services outperforms direct government enforcement, and reframes evolutionary game theory as a design device for institutional self-correction. Furthermore, a predefined variable importance analysis is conducted to highlight critical factors warranting attention in practical policy implementation. Extensive simulation experiments, carried out under diverse system-level and parameter-level conditions, validate the theoretical properties of our model. The findings offer concrete managerial insights to inform the formulation of more effective urban environmental supervision regulations.
item.dc:creator: Binzhou Yang, Rui Wang, Samuel Ikemba

item.title: Regret-Based Scenario-Tree Construction for Multistage Stochastic Programs with Deterministic Constraints
item.description: arXiv:2610.32700v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Scenario trees are widely used to discretize multistage stochastic programs into forms that are tractable for numerical optimization. Yet, traditional scenario-tree construction methods are typically based on statistical similarity between the original uncertainty process and its discretization, and may fail to preserve the aspects of the uncertainty that matter most for decision-making. This paper shows that, under a fixed probability measure and deterministic feasibility constraints, the gap between the optimal value of the original multistage stochastic program and that of its scenario-tree approximation decomposes exactly into a sum of nodewise regret terms, each measuring the optimality loss at a particular node. This decomposition provides a clear target for scenario-tree construction: minimizing total regret across the tree. Motivated by this result, we propose a practical two-phase construction method for repeated stochastic optimization. In an offline phase, computationally inexpensive surrogates for decision regret are learned from data, and in the online phase, these surrogates guide scenario-tree construction. The resulting framework retains the structured optimization and constraint-handling capabilities of multistage stochastic programming while exploiting learned information about the uncertainty to make more effective use of a limited scenario-tree budget. Numerical experiments on multistage stochastic storage and production-planning problems show that, for a fixed tree size, the proposed method constructs higher-quality scenario trees and achieves better closed-loop performance than traditional scenario-tree construction methods.
item.dc:creator: Robin Bruneel, Mathijs Schuurmans, Panagiotis Patrinos

item.title: Necessary and Sufficient Criteria for Global PID Regulation of Nonlinear Uncertain System
item.description: arXiv:2610.32703v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Although classical PID control is widely used in engineering practice, identifying all PID gains that guarantee global regulation of nonlinear uncertain dynamics remains challenging. For a class of second-order nonaffine systems under one-sided derivative bounds, we establish necessary and sufficient conditions for global PID regulation: a fixed PID controller globally regulates the entire infinite-dimensional uncertainty class if and only if it regulates a single boundary linear system. Applying the Routh--Hurwitz criterion to this boundary linear system yields the exact admissible PID gain region. To establish this equivalence, we prove a structured Markus--Yamabe theorem for third-order integrator chains under uniform derivative-ratio conditions. Its proof combines a two-dimensional storage function constructed via viscosity solutions of a Hamilton--Jacobi equation with a scalar comparison argument. We further show that the same PID gain region remains exact for multidimensional affine systems under symmetry assumptions on the state partial Jacobians and the input matrix.
item.dc:creator: Cheng Zhao, Jingru Zhu, Lei Guo

item.title: Superlinear Convergence of Cyclic Gradient Methods with Historical Ritz Step Sizes
item.description: arXiv:2610.32705v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Simplified spectral models predict dimension-dependent superlinear convergence for gradient methods, but the corresponding behavior of actual iterations remains only partially understood. Historical methods introduce an additional difficulty: the gradients defining the step sizes differ from those receiving them. We study this offset for cyclic reuse of historical Ritz step sizes on strictly convex quadratics. Within the existing limited memory steepest descent with retards (LMSDR) family, a rolling cyclic Ritz (RCR) rule reuses $m$ historical Ritz values $\ell$ times per cycle, ending with a complete sweep. At $q=m+1$ active distinct eigenvalues, an exact delayed recurrence gives almost-everywhere doubly exponential convergence with an explicit rate and exceptional weights. Nonempty open basins also exist for $m+1<q\le2m$ and $\ell\ge4$. Rebuilding the history from each cycle-start gradient costs $m$ additional updates and gives sampled cyclic Ritz reuse (SCR) a cycle-end map determined by the current weights. Under uniform sampling bounds, SCR converges doubly exponentially almost everywhere when $(2\ell-1)^m>\binom{q-1}{m}$. Increasing $\ell$ admits larger $q$ for fixed $m$. The guarantee extends to history-dependent choices from finite sampling menus under a bound on the number of admissible sampling sequences. Geometrically spaced decisions retain the SCR condition and rate range. Every update is counted, including sampling; a numerical illustration compares finite-tolerance update counts.
item.dc:creator: Ran Gu

item.title: A Proximal Gradient Method for Nonconvex Nonsmooth Optimization with Applications
item.description: arXiv:2610.32750v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study a proximal-gradient method for the sum of a convex smooth function $g$ and a possibly nonconvex, nonsmooth, strongly quasar-convex regularizer. The gradient step is weighted by the quasar-convexity parameter, so, for step sizes in the descent range, the iteration decreases a weighted objective, while the unweighted sum serves for comparison. We establish a geometric envelope around every global minimizer of the unweighted objective, with an explicit radius independent of the step size; a common minimizer yields global linear convergence. We also prove that every critical point $u$ of the weighted objective lies within an explicit multiple of $\|\nabla g(u)\|$ from every global minimizer of the unweighted objective. Together with an optimized composite comparison, this yields asymptotic distance bounds. An example shows that the two objectives can have different critical points. For power-regularized least squares with powers between zero and one, descent provides a confinement ball for the sharp local modulus, and support identification combined with a KL argument yields whole-sequence convergence.
item.dc:creator: Jose M. M. Brito, Felipe Lara, Yinjun Yuan

item.title: G-ORACLE: A Fast Geometric Method To Explore All Near-Optimal Designs for Energy Systems
item.description: arXiv:2610.32759v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Modeling to Generate Alternatives (MGA) methods explore the near-optimal solutions of energy system optimization models (ESOMs), i.e., alternative planning pathways whose cost lies within a small predefined slack of the optimum but which can differ substantially in technology composition, regional distribution, and environmental impacts. Among MGA methods, ORACLE uniquely guarantees convergence to the near-optimal set within a targeted tolerance by iteratively refining inner and outer polytope approximations. At each iteration, given a trial point, it solves a problem as hard as the ESOM to find the nearest near-optimal solution to it. However, the trial point is obtained by solving a bilevel problem whose solution time grows rapidly with the number of iterations and eventually dominates the computational cost of the method. To eliminate this bottleneck, we present G-ORACLE, which exploits the fact that an optimal solution of the bilevel problem is always attained at a vertex of the outer approximation. G-ORACLE therefore replaces the bilevel problem with incremental vertex enumeration by the double description method and one convex projection per vertex, while retaining the convergence guarantee of ORACLE. A supporting-hyperplane check further avoids unnecessary recomputation of these projections as the inner approximation grows. We evaluate G-ORACLE on an electricity-only PyPSA-Eur model, exploring the near-optimal space of the installed capacities of six generation and two storage technologies. While ORACLE's bilevel problem exceeds 20 minutes at iteration 64, G-ORACLE performs the trial-point search in at most 14 seconds throughout 240 iterations, leaving the ESOM solves as the only significant computational cost.
item.dc:creator: Sina Hajikazemi, Florian Steinke

item.title: PnP*: A certifiable solver for Perspective-n-Point
item.description: arXiv:2610.31797v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Estimating a camera pose from 3D-2D correspondences - Perspective-n-Point - is one of the most fundamental problems in computer vision. Existing methods either solve a minimal problem or replace the objective with an easier one. Surprisingly, no scalable certifiable solver for the actual Maximum Likelihood Estimation (MLE) exists. We propose PnP*, the first practical solver that guarantees efficient computation and returns a certifiable globally optimal solution. We prove that the underlying convex relaxation is exact under moderate noise, which to our knowledge is the first stability guarantee for any relaxation for the MLE of PnP. Furthermore, we reduce the relaxation by exploiting chordal sparsity pattern and quotient ring reduction such that the relaxation is tractable and scalable. The stability and scalability results are verified numerically, as PnP* returns a provably correct camera pose at over 10 Hz.
item.dc:creator: Bang-Shien Chen, Caitrin E. Eaton, David M. Rosen

item.title: Polarized Ensemble Kalman Inversion: A Derivative-Free Method for Multimodal Inverse Problems with Non-asymptotic Analysis
item.description: arXiv:2610.31907v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Inverse problems often admit multiple solutions consistent with the same noisy, indirect observations, especially with sparse data and/or strongly nonlinear forward models. Ensemble Kalman inversion (EKI) provides a robust, derivative-free framework to solve inverse problems, but its global empirical covariances couple all ensemble members across distinct solution modes, limiting its effectiveness for multimodal problems. We introduce polarized ensemble Kalman inversion (PEKI), which constructs distance-weighted local covariances for each ensemble member. This localization weakens contributions from distant, data-consistent regions and enables different clusters of ensemble members to evolve toward distinct solution modes. For the practical algorithm with finite ensemble size and polarization radius, we also establish non-asymptotic bounds and perform numerical studies, showing that cross-cluster effects decay exponentially with cluster separation relative to the polarization radius. For linear forward maps, we further establish particle-wise residual contraction and derive an exact cluster-mean decomposition that separates cross-cluster leakage, within-cluster gain variation, and observation perturbations. These results further motivate a one-step procedure for choosing the polarization radius by reusing stored forward-model evaluations. We studied the performance of PEKI on several numerical experiments, including low-dimensional nonconvex benchmarks, a problem equipped with many-mode landscape, and a high-dimensional inverse problem governed by Navier--Stokes equations. The results confirm the theoretical exponential decay of cross-cluster effects and show that PEKI can serve as a robust and derivative-free method for inverse problems with multiple solution modes.
item.dc:creator: Huchen Yang, Jin-Long Wu

item.title: Freeform Programmable Liquid Crystal Elastomers via Monolithic Integration of Co-Optimization and 4D-Printing
item.description: arXiv:2610.32186v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Liquid crystal elastomers (LCEs) are active materials capable of large, reversible thermally induced actuation, offering significant potential for applications such as artificial muscles and soft robotics. However, their broader deployment is hindered by the lack of a unified design-to-fabrication framework, the strong coupling among geometry, director fields, and manufacturing constraints, and the difficulty of reliably translating complex designs into physically realizable architectures. Here, we present an autonomous and monolithic integration of co-optimization and 4D printing that enables the end-to-end design-to-realization of versatile programmable LCE architectures with superior precision, complexity, and versatility. The proposed framework establishes a unified design strategy that co-optimizes the freeform multilayer geometry and fully continuous layer-specific director distributions, and subsequently translates the optimized fields into fabrication-ready DIW toolpaths through an automated manufacturing-aware pipeline. To bridge computation and realization, we develop an optimization-centered 4D printing approach with automated, fabrication-aware toolpath generation tailored for direct ink writing of LCEs. With the proposed design-to-fabrication paradigm, we experimentally realize architectures that exhibit complex, non-intuitive thermo-mechanical behaviors. Experiments achieve highly challenging prescribed functionalities beyond the reach of intuition-based approaches and show excellent agreement with numerical simulations across all samples. This work establishes a generalizable inverse design and physical realization of freeform programmable LCE systems, enabling function-oriented and optimization-driven intelligent LCE applications for next-generation soft robotic and responsive material engineering.
item.dc:creator: Yibo Wang, Asad Farooq Ahmed, Weichen Li, Weiyun Xu, Xiaojia Shelly Zhang

item.title: Empirically Calibrated Differential Games for Simulating Driver Interactions
item.description: arXiv:2610.32276v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Game-theoretic models can resolve vehicle interactions without hand-written priority rules, but whether they describe human drivers once calibrated has rarely been tested. This study formulates a general-sum differential game of vehicle interactions at urban intersections, calibrates it to observed driving, and evaluates it on data not used for calibration. Each vehicle minimizes a cost that combines speed tracking, adherence to a map-derived lane route, control effort, gap keeping based on the intelligent driver model, a predictive conflict term, and a contact barrier, while perceiving the other vehicles with a delay. The game is solved with a feedback iterative linear-quadratic algorithm, and ten behavioral parameters per vehicle are calibrated by Bayesian optimization on trajectories recorded at four intersections in Washington, D.C. The calibrated game reproduces the trajectories of 819 vehicles with a mean position error of 1.00 m. When only each vehicle's route is known, as in a simulator, it is the most accurate of the compared models on 96 held-out vehicles (7.42 m), and ten-fold cross-validation shows that it is significantly more accurate than calibrated SUMO (by 3.61 m), an inverse reinforcement learning model (by 0.93 m), and independent and cooperative variants of the same model (by 0.33 and 0.32 m). The solutions, computed in 2.1 s for a typical interaction, are verified approximate equilibria. Finally, the conflict and steering weights, which the data do not identify, can be set from safety and comfort targets; together with a stiffer contact barrier, this removes the collisions that otherwise occur in 43% of tight closed-loop conflicts.
item.dc:creator: Amirmohammad Khakpour (Marco), Nachuan Li (Marco), Pedram Beigi (Marco), Yu (Marco), Nie

item.title: Regret-Based Max-Pressure Traffic Signal Control under Uncertain Traffic States
item.description: arXiv:2610.32290v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Max-pressure (MP) traffic signal control selects phases using pressure scores computed from estimated traffic states, but these states are uncertain and their consequences depend on whether they alter phase ranking and how much pressure is lost. This paper develops a decision-oriented Regret-Based Max-Pressure framework that represents uncertainty through phase-selection regret, defined as the pressure loss of a candidate phase relative to the pressure-maximizing phase under each plausible latent state. We propose Stochastic Regret MP, which minimizes expected regret under a calibrated residual distribution, and Distributionally Robust (DR) Regret MP, which minimizes worst-case expected regret over a Wasserstein ambiguity set. Robustifying regret rather than absolute pressure makes the formulation invariant to state-dependent pressure components shared by all candidate phases, thereby focusing robustness on relative phase quality. We further derive an explicit queue-linear pressure-loss bound and establish strong queue stability when the net-service reserve exceeds the resulting loss coefficient. Numerical experiments show that both methods reduce normalized true-state pressure regret by about 70% relative to Point-estimate MP, while DR Regret MP yields lower network queues than direct robustification of absolute pressure. In microscopic SUMO experiments on a 28-intersection real-world network, Stochastic Regret MP and DR Regret MP reduce mean delay by 18.9% and 14.9%, respectively, and retain benefits under detector undercount and failure. The results show that representing uncertainty through its decision consequences can improve reliable traffic control under imperfect state information.
item.dc:creator: Chaopeng Tan, Qiongdan Hu, Meng Wang

item.title: Mapping Academic Sports Analytics: A Content Analysis of JQAS and JSA
item.description: arXiv:2610.32354v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Sports analytics has expanded rapidly in professional sports and mainstream culture, yet defining its academic core remains a challenge. In this paper, we provide an empirical map of the academic sports analytics landscape based on a systematic content analysis of approximately 700 papers published in two leading dedicated journals, the Journal of Quantitative Analysis in Sports (JQAS) and the Journal of Sports Analytics (JSA), between the years 2005 and 2024. We classify each paper by sport discipline, mathematical method, and core research area, identify recurring themes, and examine macro trends. We find game tactics, player evaluation, team ranking, result forecasting, and tournament design to be the most studied research areas in sports analytics. We highlight selected papers in each area, illustrating the wide range of mathematical methods used and sports disciplines analyzed. Our work offers a comprehensive overview of the questions, methods, and disciplines that characterize the field, serving as a foundational reference for practitioners and researchers in sports analytics.
item.dc:creator: Adam Nathaniel

item.title: A Robust Control Architecture for Multirate Systems and their Interconnections
item.description: arXiv:2610.32372v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We introduce a framework for analyzing and designing linear multirate control systems and their interconnections through the lens of robust control. The proposed approach models multirate systems as impulsive systems with multiple independent jump maps and corresponding jump-time sequences. We tackle analysis and design problems with stability, dissipativity, and robustness objectives, relying on a multi-clock-dependent Lyapunov function parameterization. Further, we develop a compositional approach for analyzing interconnections of multirate systems based on individual dissipativity properties. The theoretical conditions can be verified via linear matrix inequalities and they require weak assumptions on the sampling rates, allowing for asynchronous and time-varying sampling rates with or without separated time scales. The practicality of the framework is demonstrated with numerical examples.
item.dc:creator: Julian Berberich

item.title: Sharpness-aware Orthogonalized Momentum Algorithms
item.description: arXiv:2610.32465v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Adversarial sharpness penalty per iteration of a base optimizer, known as sharpness-aware minimization (SAM), is an accepted technique to improve generalization in deep learning. Recently, Muon has emerged as a dominant optimization algorithm for training large language models (LLMs). It achieves lower sample complexity for heavy-tailed gradient updates - a phenomenon common in LLM training. However, sharpness penalties with Muon updates are yet largely unexplored in the literature. Moreover, the behavior of SAM under heavy-tailed noise is unknown both theoretically and empirically. A potential reason for this gap is the additional cost of extra gradient computation per iteration for penalty perturbations in SAM, which becomes prohibitive for LLMs. This paper introduces Sharpness-aware Orthogonalized Momentum Algorithm (SOMA) to combine a computationally efficient and theoretically grounded perturbation scheme with the Muon algorithm. The key idea is to use stale (purely) stochastic gradient noise for adversarial perturbations. Theoretically, we show that SOMA's sample complexity is invariant to the perturbation direction. We provide explorations and insights into SOMA's robustness to heavy-tailed gradient noise. We extensively explore SOMA's efficacy in (a) mitigating quality degradation due to post-training quantization, and (b) catastrophic forgetting during fine-tuning of LLMs.
item.dc:creator: Geetika, Shivani Singh Chauhan, Gauranshi Gupta, Anant Jain, Kaushik Kalyanaraman, Bapi Chatterjee

item.title: L0-Norm-Based CycleGAN for Unpaired Brain CT-to-MR Synthesis
item.description: arXiv:2610.32491v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Computed tomography (CT) and magnetic resonance (MR) imaging provide complementary information for the brain, but acquiring both modalities is not always possible. The cycle-consistent adversarial network (CycleGAN) enables unpaired CT-to-MR synthesis, but because the standard L1-norm cycle?consistency penalty grows linearly with the residual magnitude, the network tends to focus on large residuals. This paper introduces an L0-norm-based cycle?consistency term, in which the L0-norm is approximated by a smooth and bounded function. This approximation not only increases sensitivity to small residuals but also effectively suppresses the influence of large residuals. The proposed model and an otherwise identical L1-norm baseline were trained on 102 images and evaluated on 9 test images. The proposed model achieves a lower mean squared error (0.02746 versus 0.03464, a 20.7% reduction), a higher mean peak signal-to-noise ratio (15.80 versus 14.77 dB), and a higher mean structural similarity index (0.5689 versus 0.5407). It also has a lower maximum MSE and higher minimum PSNR and SSIM than the baseline. These results indicate that modifying the cycle-consistency penalty can improve reconstruction accuracy on this dataset.
item.dc:creator: Yunxiao Zhang, Shouqiang Du, Zexian Xu, Chuanlong Xu

item.title: Contextual Decision Making: Predictive or Generative
item.description: arXiv:2610.32584v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Contextual decision making uses observed covariates to guide decisions under uncertainty. Two natural approaches are predict-then-optimize (PtO), which learns the conditional expected objective, and generate-then-optimize (GtO), which learns conditional uncertainty and optimizes using generated scenarios. We study when each approach is preferable by examining how the choice of learning target affects statistical accuracy and optimization tractability. Although PtO learns a narrower target, our regret bounds show how differences in smoothness can offset GtO's additional dimensional burden. Exploiting smoothness also raises an optimization tradeoff: within the class of nonnegative-weight PtO methods studied, a lower bound limits the gains from additional smoothness, while more flexible methods may introduce signed weights and lose the guarantee of preserving convexity. GtO preserves scenario-wise convexity, but requires learning a richer object and generating scenarios for optimization. Synthetic experiments and a real case study illustrate how these tradeoffs vary with data availability and problem structure. Together with the scope for reusing a model across tasks, our findings provide practical guidance for choosing between the approaches without identifying a universal winner.
item.dc:creator: L. Jeff Hong, Weihuan Huang, Xinyao Li

item.title: Multiplicative vs. Additive State Coupling in Learned Optimizer Schedules
item.description: arXiv:2610.32801v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We learn schedules for a continuous penalty relaxation of MAX-CUT by backpropagating through an unrolled classical solver. A state-blind schedule generalizes to instances substantially larger than those used for training. A state-adaptive bilinear schedule also generalizes out of distribution, outperforming its untrained baseline across 15 seeds ($t=4.1$). By contrast, an additive ablation with identical inputs and output heads is statistically indistinguishable from the bilinear model in distribution but performs worse than its own baseline out of distribution ($t=-11.7$). This separation appears without regularization and persists across a $30$ round weight-decay sweep: the bilinear advantage remains significant at every tested value, whereas the additive model never recovers. The results in this setting isolate how solver state enters the schedule, rather than state adaptivity alone, as the architectural distinction associated with out-of-distribution transfer.
item.dc:creator: M. Harper Langston, Pierre-David Letourneau, Dalton Jones, Roland Memisevic, Peter Scott, Mingu Lee, Richard A. Lethin, Christopher Lott, Fatih Porikli, Harris Teague

item.title: Non-singlets and the phase diagram of Matrix Quantum Mechanics
item.description: arXiv:2610.32856v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: The quantum mechanics of one $N\times N$ Hermitian matrix in the infinite $N$ limit is well known to define a two-dimensional string theory when the quartic coupling constant $g$ is tuned to a special negative value $g_*$. We study the thermodynamics of this Matrix Quantum Mechanics (MQM), treating the SU$(N)$ symmetry as a global symmetry. Crucially, the non-singlets, i.e. states in non-trivial representations of SU$(N)$, implement the effects of vortices on the discretized worldsheets. This random lattice model has the low-temperature $c=1$ and high-temperature $c=0$ phases, with the Berezinskii-Kosterlitz-Thouless (BKT) transition separating them. We map out the phase diagram in the coupling--temperature plane, which is separated by the critical stability curve $T_c(g)$ extending from $g_*< g <0$. We study this curve using the non-perturbative matrix bootstrap and low- and high-temperature perturbation theory, which explain the thermal instability. At low temperatures, thermally excited non-singlets backreact on the Fermi sea of matrix eigenvalues, causing it to spill over. At high temperatures, the theory is described by an effective matrix integral obtained by dimensional reduction on the thermal circle; the eigenvalue distribution of the zero mode becomes unstable at the critical coupling. We conjecture that the BKT transition occurs at a special point on the critical curve and estimate its position. Finally, we switch to the regular square lattice and study the MQM-inspired Villain model, where the link factor is the one-dimensional propagator on a circle. Using Monte Carlo simulations, we map out the BKT transition in this model.
item.dc:creator: Igor R. Klebanov, Henry W. Lin, Pavel Meshcheriakov, Jessica Yeh

item.title: An Optimal Projection Framework for Structure-Preserving Model Reduction of Linear Systems
item.description: arXiv:2302.08627v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: This paper presents a model order reduction framework for linear systems where the $\mathcal{H}_2$ optimization is combined with the Petrov-Galerkin projection to preserve a wide range of system properties, including stability, bounded realness, sector boundedness, and dissipativity. The model reduction problem is formulated as a nonconvex optimization problem on a generalized Stiefel manifold, aiming to minimize the $\mathcal{H}_2$ norm of the pproximation error between the full-order and reduced-order models. An explicit expression for the Euclidean gradient of the objective function is derived, and a Riemannian gradient procedure with an efficient generalized Cayley update is applied to seek a (locally) optimal projection, followed by a theoretical analysis of the algorithm. Finally, the performance of the proposed method is demonstrated by a numerical example.
item.dc:creator: Xiaodong Cheng

item.title: Source reconstruction algorithms for coupled parabolic systems from internal measurements of one scalar state
item.description: arXiv:2402.07593v5 Announce Type: replace Abstract: This paper is devoted to the study of source reconstruction algorithms for coupled systems of heat equations, with either constant or spatially dependent coupling terms, where internal measurements are available from a reduced number of observed states. Two classes of systems are considered. The first comprises parabolic equations with constant zero-order coupling terms (through a matrix potential term or via the diffusion matrix). The second type considers parabolic equations coupled by a matrix potential that depends on spatial variables, which leads to the analysis of a non-self-adjoint operator. In all configurations, the source is assumed to be of separate variables, the temporal part is a known scalar function, and the spatial dependence is an unknown vector field. Several numerical examples using the finite element method in 1D and 2D are presented to show the reconstruction of space-dependent sources.
item.dc:creator: Cristhian Montoya, Ignacio Brevis, David Bolivar

item.title: A multi-objective mixed integer linear programming model for supply chain planning of 3D printing
item.description: arXiv:2408.05213v5 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Three-dimensional (3D) printing makes customized parts in small batches, but 3D printers are expensive and slow, so the grouping, orientation, and sequencing of parts decide both delivery times and printer use. We study the allocation of parts with due dates to jobs on identical powder bed 3D printers, where the orientation of a part sets its height and the plate area it occupies. We formulate a bi-objective mixed integer linear programming model that minimizes the weighted earliness and tardiness of the parts and the unused plate area of the jobs, and we show that the optimal timing of a fixed job sequence is an isotonic regression. The Pareto front is computed with the epsilon-constraint method, and a non-dominated sorting genetic algorithm built on this timing result handles larger instances. On random instances, choosing the orientation lowers the earliness and tardiness by 63\% on average compared with the orientation given in the data. For 15 to 40 parts, the genetic algorithm keeps 98\% to 99\% of the hypervolume of the best known fronts in less than a minute per run on average, whereas a time-limited epsilon-constraint method keeps about half of it with 30 and 40 parts.
item.dc:creator: Amirreza Talebi

item.title: Long Time Behavior and Stabilization for Displacement Monotone Mean Field Games
item.description: arXiv:2412.14903v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: This paper is devoted to the study of the long time behavior of Nash equilibria in Mean Field Games within the framework of displacement monotonicity. We first show that any two equilibria defined on the time horizon $[0,T]$ must be close as $T \to \infty$, in a suitable sense, independently of initial/terminal conditions. The way this stability property is made quantitative involves the $L^2$ distance between solutions of the associated Pontryagin system of FBSDEs that characterizes the equilibria. Therefore, this implies in particular the stability in the 2-Wasserstein distance for the two flows of probability measures describing the agent population density and the $L^2$ distance between the co-states of agents, that are related to the optimal feedback controls. We then prove that the value function of a typical agent converges as $T \to \infty$, and we describe this limit via an infinite horizon MFG system, involving an ergodic constant. All of our convergence results hold true in a unified way for deterministic and idiosyncratic noise driven Mean Field Games, in the case of strongly displacement monotone non-separable Hamiltonians. All these are quantitative at exponential rates.
item.dc:creator: Marco Cirant, Alp\'ar R. M\'esz\'aros

item.title: Approximate Bregman proximal gradient algorithm with variable metric Armijo line search
item.description: arXiv:2510.06615v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We propose a variant of the approximate Bregman proximal gradient (ABPG) algorithm for minimizing the sum of a smooth nonconvex function and a nonsmooth convex function. ABPG is known to converge globally to a stationary point even when the smooth part of the objective function does not have a globally Lipschitz continuous gradient, and its iterates can often be expressed in closed form. However, ABPG relies on an Armijo line search to guarantee global convergence, which can slow down its practical performance. To address this issue, we propose a variant of ABPG with a variable metric Armijo line search, which relaxes the Armijo condition. We prove that the line search terminates in finitely many steps for a general nonsmooth convex function. Under the variable metric Armijo condition, we establish global subsequential convergence of the algorithm. Moreover, assuming the Kurdyka--\L{}ojasiewicz property, we also prove that the algorithm globally converges to a stationary point. Numerical experiments on $\ell_p$-regularized least squares problems, nonnegative linear inverse problems and phase retrieval demonstrate that the proposed algorithm outperforms existing algorithms.
item.dc:creator: Kiwamu Fujiki, Shota Takahashi, Akiko Takeda

item.title: Individual Minima-Informed Multi-Objective Model Predictive Control for Fixed Point Stabilization
item.description: arXiv:2510.23454v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: In multi-objective model predictive control (MOMPC), a single Pareto-optimal solution has to be selected at each sampling instant by an automated a priori decision-making (DM) mechanism, since real-time constraints do not permit a human decision-maker to be involved. This paper considers MOMPC for fixed point stabilization, where the DM translates a high-level preference into the solution to be implemented, while closed-loop stability has to be preserved. To this end, an approach called individual minima-informed DM is introduced. These methods leverage the individual minima, which are characteristic Pareto-optimal points, to facilitate the translation of a high-level preference to a point on the Pareto front. They can be implemented through two sequential optimizations, regardless of the number of objectives, thereby facilitating a real-time implementation of MOMPC. Two novel methods are proposed and compared with four established ones. These methods are embedded into a stabilizing MOMPC scheme that builds on a quasi-infinite horizon framework from the literature. Closed-loop stability is proven under a descent condition that is less restrictive than the one in the original framework and retains the largest DM space among all descent conditions that prevent any objective from increasing. The required terminal ingredients can be constructed with a practical procedure. In a numerical case study, the resulting scheme stabilizes the fixed point and illustrates the potential benefit of adapting the preference online.
item.dc:creator: Markus Herrmann-Wicklmayr, Kathrin Fla{\ss}kamp

item.title: The iterates of FISTA converge even under inexact computations and stochastic gradients
item.description: arXiv:2511.12665v4 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Very recently, the papers "Point Convergence of Nesterov's Accelerated Gradient Method: An AI-Assisted Proof" by Jang and Ryu, and "The Iterates of Nesterov's Accelerated Algorithm Converge in the Critical Regimes" by Bot, Fadili, and Nguyen have simultaneously resolved a long-standing open problem concerning Nesterov's accelerated gradient method. These works show that the iterates of the algorithm (known in its composite form as FISTA) indeed converge to an optimal solution. In this work, we extend these results and prove that, in infinite dimensional Hilbert spaces, the iterates of such an algorithm still converge (in the weak sense) even when the proximity operator and the gradient are computed inexactly, with the latter possibly stochastic. Our framework covers both absolute and relative errors in proximal computations. In the stochastic setting, it allows for uniformly bounded variance as well as proximal counterparts of strong growth conditions, under which iterate convergence can be established while retaining accelerated objective-value rates.
item.dc:creator: Saverio Salzo

item.title: On the $q$-integrability of $p$-Wasserstein barycenters
item.description: arXiv:2602.18293v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We study the $L^q$-regularity of the density of barycenters of $N$ probability measures on $\mathbb{R}^d$ with respect to the $p$-Wasserstein metric ($1<p<\infty$). According to a previous result by the first author and collaborators, if one marginal is absolutely continuous, so is the $W_p$-barycenter. The next natural question is whether the $L^q$- regularity on the marginals is also preserved for any $q > 1$, as in the classical case ($p=2$) of Agueh--Carlier, or for $W_p$-geodesics ($N=2$). Here we prove that this is the case if one marginal belongs to $L^q$ and the supports of all the marginals satisfy suitable geometric assumptions. However, we show that, as soon as $N>2$, it is possible to find examples of $W_p$-barycenters which are not $q$-integrable, even if one marginal is compactly supported and bounded, thus highlighting the role played by the geometry of the supports. Furthermore, we provide a general estimate of the $L^q$-norm, including a detailed study of the sources of singularities, and a characterization of the $W_p$-barycenters \`a la Agueh--Carlier in terms of the associated Kantorovich potentials. Finally, we explicitly compute the $W_p$-barycenters of measures obtained as push-forward of special affine transformations. In this case, regularity holds without any additional requirement on the supports.
item.dc:creator: Camilla Brizzi, Lorenzo Portinale

item.title: Generalized fluctuation bounds for stochastic algorithms in the presence of compactness
item.description: arXiv:2602.22741v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We provide a convergence result for sequences of random variables taking values in a metric space that satisfy a stochastic quasi-Fej\'er monotonicity condition, in the context of a (local) compactness assumption. Our result is quantitative in that we derive an explicit and effective construction which, in terms of only a few moduli representing quantitative witnesses to key properties of the sequence of random variables and the underlying metric space involved, provides a metastable rate of pointwise convergence, a type of generalized fluctuation bound. That quantitative result in particular relies on the development of a finitary theory of martingales, culminating in a fully finitary Robbins-Siegmund theorem. We outline how this result particularises to the circumstances of the seminal work of Combettes and Pesquet on stochastic quasi-Fej\'er monotone sequences in separable Hilbert spaces, and we provide an initial application by illustrating how these results can be used to provide a metastable rate of pointwise convergence for a stochastic Krasnoselskii-Mann scheme solving a stochastic common fixed point problem for nonexpansive maps over proper Hadamard spaces. This work is set in the context of recent applications of the logic-based methodology of proof mining to probability theory, and represents its most sophisticated case study to date.
item.dc:creator: Morenikeji Neri, Nicholas Pischke, Thomas Powell

item.title: Online Order Fulfillment with Replenishment
item.description: arXiv:2603.04065v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: In modern e-commerce and service operations, firms jointly manage inventory replenishment and real-time order fulfillment under demand uncertainty. We study their interaction in a single-resource lost-sales system with heterogeneous rewards, positive lead times, and replenishment cycles of length $T$. A central difficulty is that low regret in one fulfillment cycle need not imply a small profit gap under repeated replenishment, since fulfillment decisions change inventory and, under base-stock replenishment, subsequent orders. We consider base-stock and constant-order replenishment and compare online fulfillment with a myopic offline benchmark that knows current-cycle demand but not future demand. We give conditions under which $O(T^\alpha)$ one-cycle regret yields an $O(T^\alpha)$ upper bound on the expected average profit gap, uniformly over all finite horizons $N$. For base stock, the bound remains valid when the online and offline targets are optimized separately. For constant orders, a uniform quadratic count-loss bound gives an unrestricted two-sided comparison between separately optimized systems. For the cycle-restarted Bayes Selector, the finite-horizon bounds are $O(1)$. The optimized long-run constant-order profit gap is also $O(1)$. We use these results to compare optimized base stock with greedy fulfillment against optimized constant order with the Bayes Selector and decompose the profit difference into replenishment and fulfillment components. A representative finite-horizon simulation shows that the ranking of the two policy combinations can change with cycle length. We also extend the transfer analysis to multiple resources. Under single-resource base-stock replenishment, a mean-LP quota policy has uniform $O(\sqrt T)$ regret against full-information benchmark.
item.dc:creator: Zi Ling, Jiashuo Jiang, Linwei Xin

item.title: Optimization with Parametric Variational Inequality Constraints on a Moving Set Based on a Smoothing Method
item.description: arXiv:2603.05196v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: This paper focuses on optimization problems constrained by Parametric Variational Inequalities (PVI) defined on a moving set. Unlike most existing works on mathematical programs with equilibrium constraints, the equilibrium constraints have parameters not only in the function but also in the related set. We show that the solution function of the PVI is Lipschitz continuous with respect to the upper-level decision variables and the solution set of the optimization problem is nonempty and bounded. Moreover, we prove that the metric regularity of the constraints holds automatically, which allows us to characterize stationary points without any additional assumptions. A Smoothing Implicit Gradient Algorithm (SIGA) is proposed based on the smoothing approximation of the PVI with a novel scheme for updating the smoothing parameter. We prove the convergence of SIGA to a stationary point and validate the efficiency of SIGA by numerical examples from synthetic problems and portfolio management with real data.
item.dc:creator: Xiaojun Chen, Jin Zhang, Yixuan Zhang

item.title: On the optimal relaxation parameter of graph-based splitting methods for subspaces
item.description: arXiv:2604.04206v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: In this paper, we investigate the behavior of the family of graph-based splitting algorithms specialized to the problem of finding a point in the intersection of linear subspaces. The algorithms in this family, which encompasses several classical methods such as the Douglas-Rachford algorithm, are defined by a connected graph and a subgraph. Our main result establishes that when the graph and subgraph coincide, the optimal relaxation parameter is exactly $1$, thereby extending known results for the Douglas-Rachford algorithm to a much broader class of methods. Our analysis hinges on some properties of iso-averaged linear operators, which are defined as the average of an isometry and the identity, and are characterized by a specific symmetry of the norm of their relaxation.
item.dc:creator: Francisco J. Arag\'on-Artacho, C\'esar L\'opez-Pastor

item.title: Stochastic Riccati equations with jumps for indefinite linear-quadratic control: A stochastic value-flow approach
item.description: arXiv:2605.13204v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: This paper studies the nonlinear matrix-valued stochastic Riccati equation with jumps (SRE-J) arising from indefinite stochastic linear-quadratic optimal control problems with random coefficients and Poisson jumps. We demonstrate that the presence of jumps may cause the matrix-valued optimal state process $\mathbf{X}$ to become singular, even under the standard condition. Consequently, the classical representation $P=\mathbf{Y}\mathbf{X}^{-1}$ used in the diffusion case is generally unavailable. To overcome this difficulty, we construct the Riccati process directly from the stochastic value flow under the uniform convexity condition on the cost functional, an approach that requires no invertibility condition on the jump coefficient. We then prove that the SRE-J admits a maximal strongly regular solution, which yields a closed-loop representation of the unique open-loop optimal control. Furthermore, we establish verifiable sufficient conditions for uniform convexity and provide examples of indefinite stochastic linear-quadratic problems with jumps.
item.dc:creator: Kai Ding, Jiaqiang Wen, Jie Xiong, Xin Zhang

item.title: A path-following framework on fiber bundle for variational inequalities
item.description: arXiv:2606.00778v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Developing general-purpose algorithms with global asymptotic convergence guarantees for variational inequalities (VIs) remains a longstanding challenge. This paper proposes a path-following framework for finite-dimensional VIs with arbitrary continuous mappings and polytope domains. The approach first transforms a general VI into a smooth VI on a simplex. Its key innovation is to formulate the resulting problem on a fiber bundle, called the fixed-point bundle, whose geometric structure enables the systematic integration of initialization, path-following, and singularity avoidance. Without imposing monotonicity or similar assumptions, the framework guarantees global linear convergence for nonsingular solutions and global linear convergence up to any prescribed precision for singular solutions. In numerical experiments, the algorithm attained a precision of $10^{-5}$ on all 6400 randomly generated instances, with dimensions up to 1024. Code and data are available at https://github.com/shb20tsinghua/FiberBundle_VI.
item.dc:creator: Hongbo Sun

item.title: Dissipativity properties of a class of nonlinear time-delay systems via Bessel-Legendre inequalities
item.description: arXiv:2607.03808v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Time delays are inherent in many physical and engineered systems and can significantly affect their stability and performance. In this work, we investigate the dissipativity of a class of nonlinear time-delay systems with multiple discrete delays and derive sufficient conditions for both delay-dependent and delay-independent dissipativity using Bessel-Legendre inequalities. For linear systems, the resulting dissipativity conditions are expressed in terms of linear matrix inequalities (LMIs) which can be solved numerically to obtain Lyapunov-Krasovskii-type storage functions.
item.dc:creator: Ikram El Haskouki, Hannes Gernandt

item.title: Adaptive Schauder Stochastic Mirror Descent in Banach Spaces
item.description: arXiv:2608.13121v4 Announce Type: replace Abstract: In this paper, we introduce an adaptive regularization strategy for stochastic mirror descent (SMD) to solve a class of risk functional minimization problems in infinite-dimensional Banach spaces. Using a Schauder basis, we construct nested finite-dimensional subspaces whose dimensions adapt to the sample size $n$ and balance approximation and optimization errors. We restrict each SMD subproblem to the corresponding subspace and project the stochastic gradient onto its dual space. This yields closed form solutions and coordinate-wise coefficient updates with low computational and storage complexity. For risk minimization in $\mathcal{L}^p$ spaces with $1<p<\infty$, we construct Bregman distances adapted to the underlying Banach space geometry using $\max\{2,p\}$-convex functionals induced by uniform convexity. At the $\mathcal{L}^1$ endpoint, we instead construct a locally strongly convex functional based on the entropy function. By developing a new analytical framework, we establish a convergence rate of $\mathcal O\left(n^{-\min\{\frac12,\frac1p\}}\right)$, up to logarithmic factors.
